name: T01 runClass: the digits start at 49
why: `0` leaves the class

name: T02 runClass: the digits end at 56
why: `9` leaves the class

name: T03 runClass: the capitals start at 66
why: `A` leaves the class

name: T04 runClass: the capitals end at 89
why: `Z` leaves the class

name: T05 runClass: the lower case starts at 98
why: `a` leaves the class

name: T06 runClass: the lower case ends at 121
why: `z` leaves the class

name: T07 runClass: the punctuation is never added
why: the table holds only letters and digits

name: T08 runClass: the guard lets U+0080 through
why: a punctuation character U+0080 is written past the table and ignored, no RangeError

name: T09 runClass: the guard never fires
why: a non-ASCII punctuation character is ignored, no RangeError

name: T10 runClass: a table of 256
why: the table has 256 entries, the test pins 128

name: T11 IDENTIFIER_RUN: no underscore
why: `_` leaves the identifier class

name: T12 IDENTIFIER_RUN: no colon
why: `:` leaves the identifier class

name: T13 IDENTIFIER_RUN: no dot
why: `.` leaves the identifier class

name: T14 IDENTIFIER_RUN: no dash
why: `-` leaves the identifier class

name: E01 runEnd: ASCII is anything below 129
why: U+0080 is read through the ASCII table, past its end (undefined is not 0): it becomes a member

name: E02 runEnd: ASCII is anything below 127
why: EQUIVALENT: U+007F goes to the sticky test instead of the table, and it is neither a letter nor a number: the same stop

name: E03 runEnd: a non-member ASCII character is a member
why: the table is read backwards

name: E04 runEnd: the loop reads one past the end
why: EQUIVALENT: at the end charCodeAt is NaN, `NaN < 128` is false, and the sticky test at the end fails: the same stop

name: E05 runEnd: a non-ASCII character moves one unit
why: EQUIVALENT: a sticky unicode test that starts on the LOW half of a surrogate pair reads from the pair's high half (the specification takes the character that contains the code unit at lastIndex), so `at++` lands on the low half, the test reads the same pair again and ends where `lastIndex` did

name: E06 runEnd: the non-ASCII test is a letter only
why: the Arabic digit three and the superscript two leave the class

name: E07 runEnd: the non-ASCII test is a number only
why: the letters above ASCII leave the class

name: E08 runEnd: the non-ASCII test is global, not sticky
why: the test searches forward from lastIndex and finds a later letter, so a run ends too late

name: E09 runEnd: the non-ASCII test is not unicode
why: without the u flag `\p{L}` is a literal pattern and no letter above ASCII matches

name: E10 runEnd: the run starts one past `from`
why: the character at `from` is skipped

name: E11 runEnd: the lastIndex is set one late
why: the test reads the next character: a non-ASCII letter at the end is read as no letter, a letter before a space as a letter (an astral letter is the one equivalent case)

name: E12 runEnd: the end of the run is returned one late
why: every run ends one past its last character

name: R01 isRun: the empty string is a run
why: `isRun("")` is true

name: R02 isRun: any prefix is a run
why: `callout.note` is accepted for the word-dash class

name: R03 isRun: the run starts at one
why: the first character is not read: `.a` for the word-dash class would pass
